title: Rig — AI Spend
description: What every AI coding harness on this machine used, priced at published API list rates. Money, tokens, models, projects, and the delegated share. The dropdowns narrow every panel to one harness, provider or model.

panels.title: Subscriptions — what is left, and when it comes back
Every plan on one line
panels.description: Read from the seller that meters each plan, so it falls for every device the account is signed in on. `measured` is how old the figure is: a plan is asked every few minutes, not every scrape.

defaults.noValue: No plan answered. `rig ai limits` says whether that is a signed-out harness, an expired token, or an account on no metered plan.

panels.title: Quota left, against spending it evenly
panels.description: The dashed line is the window's own clock: what would be left had you started at the reset and spent evenly to the end, 100% down to 0% and back to 100%. The solid line is what is actually left. Above the dash is ahead of pace — the quota outlasts the window. Below it, the window outlasts the quota and you run dry early. Only windows whose seller declares a length can be paced.

defaults.noValue: Nothing to pace. A window needs both a reset time and a declared length, and not every seller states one.

panels.title: All recorded
panels.description: Every dollar here is API list value: what these tokens would cost billed through the provider's API. A subscription pays a flat fee instead, so this is the value received rather than money leaving the account. Counts every session file still on disk.

panels.title: Burn rate
panels.description: Dollars of list value per hour, averaged over the last hour.

panels.title: Per million tokens
panels.description: Blended over every role. Rises when caches lapse and windows get rewritten.

panels.title: Context re-read
panels.description: Share of input-side tokens that are cache reads — the window being re-sent. A cache read is billed at about a tenth of a fresh input token, so high is cheap: the red end is a session paying full price to say the same thing again.

panels.title: Live sessions
panels.description: Harness sessions whose state file moved in the last few minutes.

panels.title: Harnesses seen
panels.description: Harnesses with session files on this machine. `rig ai doctor` lists all of them.

panels.title: Spend by token role
panels.description: cache_read is normally the largest by far: a running context is re-sent on every request, so cost is context size times request count. cache_write spikes when a prompt cache lapses and the whole window is paid for again.

panels.title: Spend by model
panels.description: The eight dearest in the window. A model is summed across whichever provider served it, so the Provider dropdown is what separates the same model bought from two sellers.

panels.title: Total by project
panels.description: Cumulative list value per project directory, all recorded history.

panels.title: Delegated versus direct
panels.description: Send enough work to subagents and most of the money stops being spent by the session you are watching.

panels.title: Model detail
panels.description: Rates come from models.dev. `rig ai models` prints the per-million figures used.

panels.title: Harnesses on this machine
panels.description: Zero files means the harness is installed but has written nothing this reader understands. `rig ai doctor` says which.

panels.title: Tokens per second by role
panels.description: reasoning is already inside output and is never priced twice.

panels.title: Context re-read share
panels.description: Climbs through a long session. The window grows and every request pays for all of it.

panels.title: Dollars per million tokens
panels.description: A step up means either a dearer model or a cache rebuild.

panels.title: Subscription window left
panels.description: What the plan has left, asked of the seller that meters it. It is the only figure on this dashboard that is about the plan rather than about list price, and it falls for every device the account is signed in on, not only this one.

defaults.noValue: No subscription here answered. `rig ai limits` says whether that is a signed-out harness, an expired token, or an account on no metered plan.

panels.title: List price against what the harness claims
panels.description: Only some harnesses report a cost at all, so the reported line covers part of the total. Where both exist the gap is the subsidy.

panels.title: Tokens with no published price
panels.description: Excluded from every dollar figure here. A model nobody sells by the token gets no invented number.

panels.title: Ledger age
panels.description: Since the exporter last read the session files.

panels.title: Price catalogue age
panels.description: models.dev is refetched by the exporter on its own schedule.
